newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir leader says Pakistan insincere about talks.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir leader says Pakistan insincere about talks.

text.p: The chief minister of India's Jammu and Kashmir state accused Pakistan on Saturday of insincerity in peace talks with New Delhi and said Islamabad will not be given an inch more of the Himalayan region.

"On the one hand Pakistan wants to have a dialogue with India, on the other hand it takes up the issue at every forum and misses no opportunity in pushing militants to our side," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Farooq Abdullah as saying.
"Pakistan would never succeed in taking away even a single inch of our land," Abdullah told a public meeting in Jammu, a Hindu enclave in India's only Moslem-majority state.
Abdullah's pro-India National Conference party is a member of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front alliance.
As foreign minister in former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government, Gujral encouraged the resumption of stalled peace talks with Pakistan in March.
Indian foreign ministry officials say Gujral has told them not to make provocative statements against Islamabad nor respond to any public criticism by Pakistan over the issue of Kashmir.
The two countries have fought two of their three wars since 1947 over Kashmir.
Pakistan wants India to hold a plebiscite in Kashmir, as sought by a 1949 United Nations resolution, to determine if its mostly Moslem citizens want to go with India or with Pakistan.
India says the two countries had agreed in 1972 to resolve the dispute bilaterally and insists that Kashmir is an integral part of India.
Gujral is due to meet Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif for rare high-level talks later this month on the margins of a South Asian leaders' meeting in the Maldives
Abdullah became chief minister of Kashmir in September last year following the first local elections there in seven years.
The polls were boycotted by Kashmir's pro-Pakistan All Party Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, Abdullah's political foe.
Gujral, visiting Jammu earlier this week, said he was not planning to hold talks with Hurriyat leaders but analysts said he left the possibility of future talks open after his meeting with Sharif.
